data.gender_notes: Birva is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Birva is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'bir', which means 'God'. This name is associated with the deity of agriculture and fertility, often invoked for prosperity and abundance. In Hindu mythology, Birva is a manifestation of Lord Vishnu, symbolizing the power of creation and nourishment. The name Birva carries the meaning “God of agriculture and fertility” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Birva usually hope their child will grow to embody god of agriculture and fertility and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: Birva is a name deeply rooted in Hindu culture and represents the reverence for the deity of agriculture and harvest time. This name is also associated with the traditional Indian celebration of 'Bhogi' or 'Bir Bass', which is a part of the Pongal festival celebrated in South India. During this celebration, a deity representing agriculture and prosperity is invoked and welcomed, often given the name Birva. The name holds great significance in rural communities as a symbol of faith, faithfulness, and the blessings of a fruitful harvest season.
data.spiritual_significance: Birva is a spiritual name steeped in the deep reverence for the divine power of creation and continuity of life. It is believed that invoking the name Birva brings prosperity, fertility and blessings to one's life. In Hindu spirituality, Birva is a manifestation of Lord Vishnu, the preserver of the universe, and represents God's hand in creating and nourishing all forms of life. It is a reminder of the interconnectedness of all things and the inherent divinity within each living being. The name Birva is a reflection of the Hindu philosophy that acknowledges and celebrates the divine in all things.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Birva: Radiant as the sun, a beacon of pure joy and inner strength. The name embodies the spirit of overcoming challenges with courage and grace.

historical_references.reference: Birva was a Bhil chieftain who led a rebellion against the British during the Indian Rebellion of 1857. He is said to have gathered a large following of fellow Bhils and other discontented locals, and successfully resisted British forces for several months before being ultimately defeated.

Birva was also a legendary figure in the Hindu epic Ramayana, renowned for his devotion to Lord Rama. He was a king of Kishkindha, a monkey kingdom, and played a crucial role in helping Rama locate and rescue his wife Sita from the demon king Ravana.
